title: Pricing authority matrix and QA-linked discounting guidelines
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a clear pricing authority matrix and operational rules that tie enterprise discount approvals to Security Questionnaire (SQ) outcomes and contract risk signals. Goal is to reduce ad-hoc discounts, accelerate legal/security review handoffs, and ensure discounts correlate with assessed risk and contract value. This ticket scopes the decision framework, approval thresholds by role, integrations required with Salesforce/CPQ and the Security QA tracker, and a rollout plan for Sales and Finance.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A documented authority matrix mapping discount bands (%), contract ARR bands, and required approvers (AE, Sales Manager, Head of Revenue, CFO, CISO) exists and is approved by Finance + Legal.
A2: Security Questionnaire (SQ) result categories (Green/Amber/Red) and their effect on discount eligibility are codified (e.g., Red customers require CISO sign-off and a cap of 10% discount).
A3: A prototype workflow in Salesforce/CPQ shows automated approver routing based on contract value and SQ RAG status (demoable to GTM).
A4: Confluence playbook published with step-by-step guidance for Sales, PS, Legal, and Security; includes example contract clauses and escalation paths.
A5: Training session scheduled for Sales leadership and Sales Ops; adoption metrics and a 30-day audit plan are defined.
proposed_steps: Step 1: Collate historical discount data (last 18 months) by deal size, ARR, and customer SQ outcome; identify outliers.
Step 2: Draft authority matrix: bands by ARR (<50k, 50-250k, 250k-1M, >1M) and discount tiers (0-5, 6-15, 16-30, >30%). Map default approvers and required legal/security approvals.
Step 3: Define SQ-to-discount rules: Green = full eligibility, Amber = cap 15% + manager approval, Red = cap 10% + CISO + Legal sign-off.
Step 4: Build a Salesforce/CPQ routing prototype (Sales Ops) that reads an SQ field (RAG) and contract ARR to enable automatic next-approver assignment and required checkboxes in the quote form.
Step 5: Publish Confluence playbook and update the Pricing & Discounts page in Drive; circulate for review to Legal, Security, Finance, and Sales leadership.
Step 6: Run 2-week shadow phase where approvals are logged but not enforced; collect feedback and tune thresholds.
Step 7: Enforce policy; monitor exceptions via weekly audit and monthly report to CFO and CISO.
